main_result: Theorem (second Kahn--Kalai conjecture, explicit form): for n>=2 and a graph H on at most n vertices with h=e(H)>=1, pc(n,H) <= min{1, 2048 e^{50} pE(n,H)(1+log2 h)}, hence pc(n,H) <= 6144 e^{50} pE(n,H) log2 n. Here pc is the density at which G(n,p) contains H with probability 1/2, and pE is the least p at which every subgraph F of H has expected copy count at least 1/2. The proof shows that a random set of density r contains a copy of H with probability at least 2/3.
proof_strategy: Set-system part (Sections 2-3): a single a-spread family is resampled by a 'transition' at a random set W of density rho = e^{50}a, and the fragment A_target minus W is shown to be small and to change measure by at most e^{11m}. Using the same W at every node of a disjoint probability tree, a potential D_v (built from local failure masses and child potentials) is shown to exceed 1 at bad nodes, its expectation is bounded by a recursion whose exponents are controlled by the factor-16 capacity growth, and Markov gives a good root with probability at least 3/4; the good nodes form a reduced tree with halved capacities and spread multiplied by at most 1/(1-e^{-m}). Iterating s = floor(log2 l_k)+1 times with fresh sets and bounding the number of attempts by 4s (geometric waiting times plus Markov) gives the tree covering theorem. Graph part (Section 4): for each edge set I, a maximizer S of sigma^{-|S|} P(S in G_I) is chosen; (F2) forces |S| < |I|/17, giving a chain of copies H_0 < H_1 < ... with capacity growth 16 and a tree whose conditional child laws are sigma-spread by maximality. Feeding this tree into the covering theorem with sigma = 128 pE yields the bound.
hardest_part: The decoupling in Lemma reduction (Steps 4-5): the same W is used at every node, and one needs that the potential D_b of a child depends only on W outside A_v(b) (via disjointness of labels along paths) so that the distortion bound (distortion inequality in Lemma local) applies to f = D_b. I checked the logic and the exponent bookkeeping (e^{-8m} and e^{12m} factors, and 12/15 - 8 <= -7), and they are consistent, but this is the step where a subtle dependence error would be easiest to miss, and I checked it by reading rather than by a full independent recomputation.

main_result: For every n≥2 and every graph H with h≥1 edges and at most n vertices, the containment threshold pc(n,H) (the density where G(n,p) contains a copy of H with probability 1/2) satisfies pc(n,H) ≤ min{1, 2048·e^50·pE(n,H)·(1+log2 h)}, where pE(n,H) is the graph expectation threshold. Since h ≤ n^2, this gives pc(n,H) ≤ 6144·e^50·pE(n,H)·log2 n. This is the second Kahn–Kalai conjecture with a single logarithm, with universal constants.
proof_strategy: Edge sets of H are built into a chain of copies H_0 ⊂ ... ⊂ H_k with each step at least 16 times larger, where each step is chosen to maximize a normalized containment ratio R_σ(I,S)=σ^{-|S|}P(S⊆G_I) (Lemma hierarchy); this forces spread of each extension law with σ=128·pE and capacities ℓ_{i+1}≥16ℓ_i. A single-family lemma (Lemma local) resamples a set via a planted-set transition at density ρ, bounding the failure probability and a change-of-measure cost; the tree version (Lemma reduction) applies this at all nodes with one common W, using a potential D_v with a recursion whose exponents are controlled by the factor-16 growth, so the root survives with probability ≥3/4 and the surviving tree has halved capacities and slightly enlarged spread. Iterating ⌊log2 ℓ_k⌋+1 successes (Theorem tree covering) with a Markov bound on attempts yields a covering at density ≤ 16e^50σ(1+log2 ℓ_k) with probability ≥2/3. I checked the one-pair computation, the intersection bound, the potential recursion and its closed form, the disjointness-based decoupling, and the spread bounds on the reduced tree; they hold as written. The parts I checked less closely are the iteration invariants and the attempt-count conditioning argument.
hardest_part: The attempt-count argument in the proof of Theorem (tree covering), Step 5, where P(Δ_i > x+1) ≤ (1/4)P(Δ_i > x) is asserted in one sentence. It needs the conditional failure bound from Lemma reduction to hold given the full history (the current tree is a random function of earlier sets), and I had to reconstruct that myself. Close behind is the decoupling in Lemma reduction Steps 4–5, which relies on D_b depending only on W outside A_v(b) and on the distortion bound applied to that D_b with a single shared W; I verified it, but only by tracing the labels through the disjointness argument.

main_result: For every n≥2 and graph H with h≥1 edges and at most n vertices, pc(n,H) ≤ min{1, 2048·e^50·pE(n,H)·(1+log2 h)}, and hence pc(n,H) ≤ 6144·e^50·pE(n,H)·log2 n. Here pc is the density at which G(n,p) contains H with probability 1/2, and pE is the least p at which every subgraph F of H has expected copy count at least 1/2. The proof shows that a random set of density r contains a copy of E(H) with probability at least 2/3.
proof_strategy: The argument has three layers. Lemma local (resampling) defines a transition: sample a source c from the spread family, then a target b with posterior weight proportional to ν_b ρ^{-|A_b|} on the event A_b ⊆ W∪A_c, and keep the fragment A_b\W. It bounds the failure probability by e^{-9m} and gives a change-of-measure bound with cost e^{11m}, using the spread hypothesis on intersections. Lemma reduction runs this transition at every node of a disjoint tree with one common W, marks nodes good or bad, and bounds a potential D_v by a recursion over levels; the factor-16 growth of capacities makes the sum converge, so the root survives with probability at least 3/4. Theorem tree covering iterates the reduction about s=⌊log2 ℓ_k⌋+1 successes, with capacities halving and spreads multiplying by less than 4, and takes 4s independent attempts. Lemma hierarchy builds the tree for H from a ratio-maximizing chain of subgraphs, and the graph-expectation threshold enters only through (F2). Final constants: 16·128=2048, and 1+log2 h ≤ 3 log2 n. I checked each inequality and constant I could reach, and found no error.
hardest_part: The potential recursion in Lemma reduction (Steps 3–6) and the iteration bookkeeping in Theorem tree covering. The first depends on the claim that D_b is a function of W\A_v(b) (Step 4) combined with the change-of-measure bound (M2), applied while the same W drives every node; I checked the logic but the reasoning is spread across several steps. The second depends on the spread products (A4) and the invariants (I1)–(I3) under trimming. I verified both but relied on my own reconstruction of the conditioning, so I trust them less than the one-pair computation.
